chapter: Touring shows and the bands he heard
title: Across the river in East Jackson
summary: The all-night gambling and party district across the river, Stamps Brothers Hotel and Brother Reed's place where Paul Gayten made him sit on the piano.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and the Prohibition-era clubs

blocks.x: And I was also doing some other things over in East Jackson, or across the river, they called it... I mentioned Mister Bradley's place over there, where we played. And there were also some Black places that we played, like Stamps Brothers Hotel. They used to have the bands come

through, Earl 'Fatha' Hines... And then they would have parties for different bands; after they finished in Jackson, they'd go across the river. Because things ran all night across the river. Everything went across the river, you know.

In fact, Paul Gayten's uncle, whose name was Brother Reed, had a place over there across the river, where they used to play Cotch (that's a three-card gambling game), and Skin, Georgia Skin, all those cold-blooded games, you know, where you bet every turn of the card. And I used to work in there with Paul... They would have four or five fights a night, you know, turn out the place. And Paul used to make me sit up on top of the piano, so if they had a fight I'd just jump over behind the piano, see. [LAUGHS HEARTILY] And I'd be safe back there!
Oh, but it was over there on an all dirt road, no pavement over there, you know. And it would rain, and it would be muddy. And we just...

Yeah, Stamps Brothers in East Jackson; Stamps Brothers Hotel. And Brother Reed... They had places all over, back off those back roads and everywhere back out in those woods, like all kinds of places running all night.
